source_status: An original polynomial seed, exponent split and one Newton correction for the standard real cube-root function. No upstream kernel or historical defect is reproduced.

technical_background.relationship: Shows practical real cube-root implementations use bit-based seeds and Newton refinement. The candidate polynomial, exponent/remainder reconstruction and numerical tolerance are independently constructed; no fdlibm source or coefficients are copied.

public_contract: One fixed verdict for every finite FP16 value and all lengths 1..131072; FP32 output; relative error at most 1e-6 for nonzero values and exact numerical zero for zero values.

coefficient_construction.method: Fit a relative-error minimax quadratic on 10,001 uniformly spaced binary64 points in [1,2] using scipy.optimize.linprog, then round each coefficient to four or three decimal places. This grid is only a seed construction method, not a proof of the target bound. An independent entire-FP16 oracle and actual GPU execution qualify the implementation.

construction_audit_scope: All 63,488 finite FP16 encodings evaluated using NumPy FP32 operations without fusion against NumPy binary64 cbrt. CPU exploration results are candidate-selection records, not GPU qualification or final independent evidence.
mechanism: Newton correction reduces the seed error quadratically but does not erase it. Decimal coefficient rounding changes the remaining correction error. FP32 arithmetic and multiplication by rounded cube roots of 2 and 4 also consume the relative error budget.
independent_qualification: Directed MPFR real cbrt at 320 bits, independent mpmath real-root check at 110 decimal digits, actual T4 execution of the full finite FP16 domain in multiple orders and offsets, separate length/tail/input-preservation/fresh-output checks.

oracle.scope: Directed mathematical intervals supply the oracle; mpmath agreement is an independent numerical cross-check. Exhaustive scalar encodings are separate from tensor indexing and GPU specialization checks.
oracle.method: Direct MPFR real cbrt with RoundDown and RoundUp; outward binary64 endpoints. Independent mpmath real cube root crosschecks every finite FP16 encoding.
oracle.independence: No candidate exponent splitting, polynomial coefficients, Newton iteration, remainder constants or FP32 reconstruction is used by the oracle.

indexing.argument: For index=program_id*BLOCK+lane, adjacent blocks cover disjoint adjacent intervals. mask index<N retains [0,N) exactly once. The full legal N range has 1..BLOCK active lanes in its last block, with int32-safe address indices.
indexing.scope: Arithmetic model of the audited source indexing, not exhaustive GPU testing of every N, address, or compiler specialization.

cpu_oracle_audit.scope: Exhaustive FP16 domain reference audit, separate from GPU arithmetic qualification.

semantic_review.trial_scope: Initial r1 only; all six pair trials completed.

trials.evidence: Manual seed estimates across the reduced interval, followed by the Newton relative-error relation; correctly accepted. No runtime evidence.
limitations: Approximate hand estimates are not a certified global error bound.

trials.evidence: Actual candidate run over every finite FP16 encoding with independent FP64 power reference.
limitations: t6 incorrectly converted input to FP32; validation rejected it. t7 repaired the input and supplied valid evidence.
t7 prints a Python dictionary rather than JSON; automated JSON parsing failed, but retained stdout and probe code supply the result.
The verdict overstates scalar enumeration as all legal input coverage. No offset, input-preservation or output-freshness tests were run, and only N=63488 was used.

trials.additional_probe: t11 checks all 2046 signed subnormals on the actual kernel.
trials.evidence: Actual-kernel nonzero scalar accuracy sweep plus separate subnormal sweep; zero behavior is supported by source analysis.
limitations: t9 excludes zeros from the error metric and does not assert their outputs; it also lacks offset, freshness and input-preservation checks.
The verdict overstates scalar enumeration as the entire legal tensor domain.
t10 is only a NumPy mantissa/Newton diagnostic; it omits reconstruction and compares least-squares coefficients, not the underlying minimax fit. It cannot independently establish GPU correctness.
Initial c3 incorrectly claimed FP16 subnormals convert to FP32 exponents below -24. Actual subnormal sweeps rebutted that claim.
Several auxiliary comments and sample-field labels are inaccurate; loop/code coverage and decisive numerical results were checked directly.

trials.evidence: Manually evaluated the seed near mantissa 1.7, estimated relative seed error around 1.2e-3 and post-Newton residual around 1.4e-6; correctly rejected. This identifies the true approximation mechanism.
limitations: The hand calculation is not an executed legal FP16 witness or a directed lower-bound proof.

trials.evidence: Actual kernel tested on every finite FP16 value; signed zeros explicitly checked. Independent qualification confirms the failure count and error magnitude.
limitations: No separate tensor storage checks, but a valid legal numerical counterexample is sufficient to reject.

trials.evidence: Actual kernel and public FP64 reference evaluated on every finite FP16 encoding; real nonzero counterexamples establish rejection.
limitations: t8 computes 0/0 for zero inputs, so max_rel is NaN. The separately printed nonzero counterexamples and 16664 threshold failures remain valid; zero behavior is not established by this metric.

t9 tests a million random operand pairs in a separate div_rn kernel, with denominator range [1,1.21). It does not exhaust the candidate denominator range or prove universal correct rounding; the final verdict overstates that auxiliary claim.
The initial c1 arithmetic incorrectly evaluates the seed at mantissa 2 as 1.36 instead of 1.26. The final rejection rests on valid executed counterexamples, not that arithmetic.

semantic_review.summary: All three methods correctly classify both cases. No observed tool-vs-no-tool or solo-vs-debate separation. No repeat is eligible under the declared first-two tool-gain rule.
semantic_review.scope_note: Model trace sweeps enumerate scalar values, not every legal tensor length, storage offset or execution. Independent private qualification separately covered 36 tensor plans and guard/storage requirements. Raw traces were not modified.
